newsitem.title: USA: US Justice probes bidding in FCC PCS airwave sales.
newsitem.headline: US Justice probes bidding in FCC PCS airwave sales.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Wednesday is it investigating possible antitrust violations among bidders in the federal government's auctioning of wireless phone licenses.

A spokeswoman said the department's antitrust division is probing "the possibility of anticompetitive conduct by bidders in connection with" the Federal Communications Commission's "auction of spectrum for PCS."
PCS refers to "personal communications services," a new generation of wireless phones.
The spokeswoman declined to say how many of the FCC's PCS auctions were under probe.
Documents obtained by Reuters show that the department is investigating possible rigging of bids.
They also show that the department is looking into whether bidders illegally schemed to divvy up the PCS licenses being sold.
